title: Urinary bladder anatomy: wall, trigone and blood supply
description: A detrusor-muscle reservoir with a smooth trigone and a two-stage sphincter.

questions.question: How does the urinary bladder store and release urine?
questions.answer: A stretchable urothelial lining and detrusor muscle allow filling. During urination, coordinated detrusor contraction and sphincter relaxation empty the bladder.

questions.question: What is the trigone of the bladder?
questions.answer: The trigone is a triangular region on the internal bladder floor between the two ureteric openings and the internal urethral opening.

questions.question: What is the detrusor muscle?
questions.answer: Three layers of interlacing smooth muscle with the wall thickened into trabeculae when obstructed. Function: Contraction empties the bladder; relaxation allows storage at low pressure.

questions.question: Where is the urothelium located?
questions.answer: Stratified transitional epithelium with umbrella cells whose plaques make it impermeable to urine. Function: A stretch-tolerant, urine-proof lining.

questions.question: What is the function of the trigone?
questions.answer: Function: Funnel for emptying; its stretch receptors trigger the micturition reflex. The smooth triangle bounded by the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice; mucosa firmly bound to muscle.
